The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(1)$ where $h(x)=f(x)+g(x).$

${h}^{′}(1)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The addition and constant multiple rules for derivatives give

$$
{h}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)+{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(1)={f}^{′}(1)+{g}^{′}(1).
$$

Also, notice that $x=1$ corresponds to

- the interval $x\in (-1,2)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (-1,2)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252554/assets/62c27964999163f87224059d85e5e6fe07a2e8b343e9fef1c34723bf9fbaaec1.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-1,2)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{1-(-2)}{2-(-1)}=1.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(1)=1.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-1,2)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{-2-1}{2-(-1)}=-1.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(1)=-1.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(1) & ={f}^{′}(1)+{g}^{′}(1) \\  & =1+(-1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
